lina: Canary run finished for mixed-quant canary (redwood-small-3b-mixedquant-v2). Setup: AWQ-int8 for attention + FP8 MLPLayer override. Test-suite: markdown -> HTML pipeline (tables, fenced codeblocks, inline code). Observed a reproducible formatting regression: HTML entities sometimes become raw tags or get partially stripped, e.g. code blocks losing escapes or closing tags dropped. sam: Can you paste a failing input + output sample? :eyes: lina: Example input (failing): ``` ```js console.log('
hi
'); ``` ``` Expected: code block preserved and inner HTML escaped. Observed output (one run): code block flattened and raw tags injected into body: `
hi` with closing tag missing. diego: I remember a similar noise with FP8 sweep last month but chalked it up to tokenizer mismatch. How consistent is this? lina: With canary seed=42 and sampling config (top_k=40, temp=0.7) we see ~12/50 failures. With seed=99 we saw 0/50. So seems seed-sensitive. maya: Could be sampling interacting with quantization boundaries. AWQ per-group quant + FP8 kernels could change logits order slightly -> different sampling path -> different formatting. But removal of closing tags sounds more like tokenization/token-id remap or truncation at group boundary. bench-bot: Canary report summary: traffic=50 requests, batch_size=4, max_new_tokens=128, sampler=top_k(40). Fail rate=24%. Affected examples concentrate on short inline HTML and fenced codeblocks with angle brackets. lina: Repro steps I'm running locally: ```bash # reproduction harness (uses same runtime binaries as canary) python tests/repro_html_preserve.py --model redwood-small-3b-mixedquant-v2 \ --seed 42 --batch 1 --sampler top_k --k 40 --max_new_tokens 128 ``` Attached failing example saved to /tmp/canary-fail-42.json sam: Any difference in tokenizer versions between our canary container and model artifacts? v1.2 -> v1.3 changes could cause merging of adjacent tokens like `
` -> single token sometimes. lina: Confirmed: model pkg contains tokenizer v1.3 but runtime environment used fallback tokenizer v1.2 in one of the compilation images. That mismatch explains some low-level tokenization differences, but doesn't fully explain tag stripping. diego: Hypothesis: (1) tokenizer mismatch moves token boundaries; (2) mixed-precision kernels have tiny logit perturbations at group boundaries; (3) deterministic sampling + beamless sampling sometimes picks partial token sequence that looks like truncated closing tag. Combine all 3 and you get observed failures. maya: Tests to run: - deterministic decode (top_k=1 / greedy) to see if sampling is the primary amplifier - enable exact tokenizer from model package in runtime image and rerun - run binary compare of token ids between AWQ-int8, GPTQ-int8, and full-fp32 on same input and seed - per-token log-prob diffs to find layer where drift crosses decision boundary lina: I'll take deterministic + tokenizer swap today. I'll also repro with pure GPTQ and with fully-FP32 baseline. bench-bot: Quick diff (first 10 tokens) between AWQ-int8 and FP32 on failing run: `awq: [1023, 45, 9, 300, 78, 4001, 17, 8]` `fp32: [1023, 45, 9, 300, 78, 4001, 17, 8]` No token id mismatch for the earliest tokens; drift shows up around token index 22 in logits (small prob differences ~1e-3). sam: If drift appears later, maybe KV cache rounding / eviction at certain sequence lengths can scramble subsequent generation. What's sequence length when failure starts? lina: Failures cluster when prefix_len ~48 and gen_len between 8-24. We saw one reproduce when KV cache boundary aligns with MLP quant-group boundary. diego: Plan of action: 1) Add html-entity-preserve checks to evallib: count '&#' / '<' / '>' tokens ratio pre/post and assert tag balancing. 2) Run layer-level kl/divergence between awq/gptq/fp32 across a sample set. 3) Temp mitigation: pin runtime tokenizer to model tokenizer in canary images, and disable mixed fp8 mlp override for next canary batch. 4) Long term: add unit test in runtime that runs small html examples through quant kernels with artificial deterministic seeds to catch this. lina: I created a canary test spec `html-escape-preserve` and added it to the canary pipeline: 100 inputs (mix of inline tags, nested tags, code fences). Threshold: fail if >1% harmful (tag imbalance / raw tags present). deploy-bot: Canary rollout update: started 10% traffic at 1767321200, currently at 10%. Monitoring logs for html-escape-drop alert. lina: Temporary rollback plan: if fail rate >5% in canary within first 30m, rollback to model-2025-06-v1 (fully FP32 serving). eva: Noted. I'll add an alert rule (prod.signal.html-escape-drop) with anomaly detection over the next 24h so we can catch any spillover to production. sam: Nice triage. If you want I can borrow the quant-probing harness to run per-layer sweep across GPUs. lina: Please do — will DM you the small dataset. I'll post artifacts here once I have deterministic repro and the first KL plots. diego: Also flagging infra: ensure the canary image's tokenizer binary is pinned in the image manifest. If it's using the fallback from shared /opt/tokenizers we should change to packaged one. lina: Good catch. I'll add a manifest check to the canary job. sam: Thanks all. Keep updates short in this thread. :thumbsup: lina: Uploaded initial repro tarball and a short summary to the canary run thread. Will follow up with numeric diffs in ~2h.
